test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem at variance from commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

Statements:

1. All couriers are shipments.

2. All shipments are transports.

3. No haul is transport.

Conclusions:

I. No transport is shipment.

II. All couriers are transports.

III. Some transports are shipments.

IV. No courier is haul.

options.text: Only conclusions II and IV follow.
Only conclusions I and IV follow.
Only conclusions II, III and IV follow.

solution:
**Given Statements:**

1. All couriers are shipments.

2. All shipments are transports.

3. No haul is transport.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc5b0f3e71cf131bc2a9fe5c466e494f5e49e9440fd849064316858b71fef426.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. No transport is shipment → False (Because it is given that all shipments are transports which means some part of transport is definitely shipment.)

II. All couriers are transports → True (Because it is given that all couriers are shipments and all shipments are transports which gives all couriers are transports)

III. Some transports are shipments → True (Because it is given that all shipments are transports which means some part of transport is definitely shipment.)

IV. No courier is haul → True (Because there is no relation given between courier and haul, so it can be possible but not definitely true)

So, conclusion II, III, and IV follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.
